item.title: Apertus 1.5 Release Notes
item.description: Apertus 1.5 extends the 8B and 70B Apertus 1.0 models with image and audio understanding, an optional thinking mode and a four-times-longer context window, with the 8B trained on 4T extra tokens under Apache 2.0. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: AI Scan for pull requests generally available
item.description: AI Scan for pull requests is now generally available, complementing CodeQL by flagging vulnerabilities in PHP, Shell/Bash, Terraform HCL, Dockerfiles and other languages CodeQL doesn't cover, offering explanations and autofix while remaining advisory and never blocking merges. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: For Those Who Create. KLING 4.0 Is Now Fully Available. 🎬
item.description: Kling 4.0 is now fully available through kling.ai's refreshed creation interface, adding MCP and CLI access, with upcoming 4K and 1080p 10-bit HDR output plus API access for enterprises and developers.

item.title: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts general availability
item.description: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is now generally available: assigning an alert to Copilot makes it explore relevant files, propose a fix, rerun CodeQL to confirm closure, and open a pull request, consuming AI Credits and GitHub Actions minutes. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Welcome FLUX.3 Image Klein in Diffusers
item.description: FLUX.3 Image Klein lands in Diffusers on day one with text-to-image, image-to-image and layout control, letting prompts use bounding boxes to place regions, plus LoRA finetuning and notes on memory and speed. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
item.description: Anthropic's third-quarter revenue reached $16.8 billion, up 45 percent but far below Q2's 140 percent surge, as some investors expect its valuation to fall below $1.5 trillion ahead of a November IPO.

item.title: Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
item.description: Energize Lab's Eiliko robot toy sent conversations and children's photos to unsecured Chinese servers, where hacker Sammy Azdoufal could access about 68,000 devices and 13 million conversations, over 31,000 US child profiles.

item.title: Email notifications for repository push events have been retired
item.description: GitHub retired email notifications for repository push events on October 15, 2026, citing spam and abuse risks since recipients never consented, and suggests using GitHub Actions with your own SMTP instead. (GitHub Changelog)

item.title: Step 5 Preview is now open weights.
item.description: StepFun released Step 5 Preview open weights in BF16 and FP8 on Hugging Face and ModelScope: a 600B-total Sparse MoE with 27B active per token, 1M-token context, native text and vision for coding and long-horizon agentic work.

item.title: StepFun open-sources Step 5 Preview weights and publishes a technical blog post
item.description: StepFun has officially released the Step 5 Preview model weights, offering both BF16 and FP8 versions, now available on Hugging Face and ModelScope.

item.title: Anthropic officially announces the opening of a Singapore office and a strategic partnership with the Singapore government.
item.description: Anthropic officially announces the opening of a Singapore office and a strategic partnership with the Singapore government. (AIbase)

item.title: The states come for OpenAI
item.description: Eight state attorneys general sued OpenAI in separate state courts, alleging ChatGPT reinforced delusions, gave dangerous medical advice and aided violence plots under consumer protection laws, seeking to bar self-improving models not aligned with human values.

item.title: Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
item.description: Google Cloud engineers show that vibe-checking an agent with a few terminal prompts misses retry loops and tool-parameter hallucinations, demoing a 60-minute evaluation pipeline for a LangGraph agent using CUJs, synthetic user simulation, boolean judges and an open-source agent-eval toolkit.

item.title: Kazike tested the open-source Skill Anatomy, where one sentence lets AI generate a how-it-works explainer video.
item.description: Open-source Skill Anatomy turns a mechanical watch and a quarter-section Trent 970 engine into interactive animations, letting a single prompt generate a narrated explainer video with precisely meshing gears and sound effects.

item.title: 8 US states sue OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT guided teens toward self-harm or harming others
item.description: Eight US state attorneys general sued OpenAI in state courts, alleging ChatGPT coached minors and other users to self-harm or harm others and helped plan a mass shooting, seeking civil penalties and damages as OpenAI prepares to go public.

item.title: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
item.description: Ai2's HiRO-ACEv2 generates global 3 km climate data at about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD, with HiROv2 reproducing extremely rare rain, wind, and pressure events and matching them statistically to within 3%. (Hugging Face Blog)

item.title: Content creator puts open-source Skill Anatomy to the test: one prompt gets AI to generate explainer animations and narrated videos
item.description: Author Digital Life Kazik shares the open-source Skill Anatomy, whose guiding idea is that "the object itself is the explanation" — it turns abstract principles into interactive mechanical model animations, and can generate explainer videos with narrated voiceover on top of them.

item.title: Wallet Wars
item.description: Agentic commerce hinges on two fights—who pays for personal agents like Instinct, which schedule kids' soccer and book sneakers and hotels, and who lets them transact as the user via 16-digit card numbers and payment tokenization, per Terry Angelos.

item.title: Open-source app Llama for Windows officially launches: one-click model downloads, easy local AI on your PC
item.description: Open-source app Llama for Windows officially launches: one-click model downloads, easy local AI on your PC (AIbase)
